task_prompt: Would you live in a place that is always warm?
response_text:
Living someplace constantly warm would be nice at first, but would get old after a while. I would live somewhere that cycles through all four seasons because it is easier to remain comfortable in colder weather, I would be able to enjoy winter acitivities, and frequent heat being too boring.

Feeling constant sweat on one's body or being unable distract oneself from the non-stop heat they might be feeling can become very stressful. Being someone who is easily overwhelmed, these conditions do not appeal to me. Additionally, it is much easier to adjust one's comfort regarding temperature when it's colder rather than warmer. Being too cold has simple fixes: dress in warmer clothes, or layer up! However, you can only take so much off when too hot. This makes it easier to keep comfortable in unfavourable weather conditions sided towards cold weather rather than warm. As well as physical comfort, emotional comfort is also a factor. In many tropical places, Florida for example, dangerous hurricanes and storms are not uncommon. This would leave me living in a constant state of fear. 

     Not only is it a matter of comfort, but a matter of fun. Living someplace constantly warm leaves one missing out on enjoyable winter activities. Skiing, skating, and sledding are all sports only available during the winter. These are some of my favourite things to do, and I would hate to be unable to participate in them. Regarding school, one of the best aspects of winter is the snow days. Without any snow during the winter, snow days are obviously impossible. Winter loses it's charm because of this and makes school feel too long. Finally, hot drinks and food are some enjoyable parts of cold winter weather. There's nothing better than spending all day outside in the snow, and coming in to a steaming cup of hot chocolate, or eating a beavertail after a long day of skating on the canal. Hot drinks and meals would lose their comforting feeling if one was living in someplace always warm. 

     Lastly, constant heat get boring. 'Sweater weather' is the most comfortable time of year for me. Being able to dress cozily while not being too hot or too cold makes autumn very enjoyable. I wouldn't want to miss out on this perfect weather. Speaking of sweaters, fashion is much more versatile during colder seasons. Living in constant heat means shorts and a t-shirt everyday. Although it might be more convenient to dress that way, it certainly wouldn't be the most stylish. Cold weather gives the opportunity to be creative with one's style. Finally, living in warm weather would get too repetitive. I would begin to feel very drained and detatched living in the same weather conditions every single day, and may have difficulty seperating days from one another.

This has an effect on Canada's ecosystem as invasive species can ruin environments just as fast as they entered. Once a specie has established itself there, it's hard to get rid of it. Invasive species have no natural predators in the environment they're consindered invasive, since many of them come abroad on boats/ships entering the country. Secondly, endangered animals are also affected by climate change. Some reasons are because of increased amount of predators or a decrease in prey  because of invasive species. Many animals may find it difficult to adapt to the new climate and as a result die.

Lastly, climate change affects habitats of many animals, like animals in the Arctic. For example, Polar Bears and Penguins are affected by the warming climate. As they mainly live on ice glaciers, with climate change many glaciers continue to melt which destroys their habitat. Not only does this affect animals, but it can also affect us humans. Climate change can cause an increased amount of natural disasters like floods or tsunamis. Coastal regions of many countries are impacted by this. An increased amount of floods mean more money being spent on repairing cities affected. It can also cause unpredictable weather which also can affect people.

In conclusion I believe climate change is important to care about because it affects how we live on this planet, and how many other animals live on this planet.
